citation.title: Novel Artificial Neural Network Aided Structural Topology Optimization
citation.authors: Xiangrui Kong; Yuching Wu; Peng Zhu; Peng Zhi; Qianfan Yang

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The paper reports that FE computation takes over 90% of the SIMP run time but about 40% of the neural-assisted method's run time, as a proxy for reduced computational cost.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: The percentages are shares of each method's own runtime; total classical and ML runtimes are not printed, so no overall speed factor follows.
claim.alternatives: §6 says final structural performance differs by less than 10% and efficiency improves; §5.1–5.4 shows objective curves and FE time shares for multiple meshes.

baseline.solver: sparse matrix equation solver, type not stated (§5.4)
baseline.problem_size: 2D grids including 60 × 60, 120 × 120, 240 × 240 and 480 × 480 elements for timing-share plots (§5.4, Figs. 13–14)
baseline.classical_iterations: 20 iterations fixed in the numerical examples (§4.4–4.5); most examples converge in 10–20 steps (§5.1, Fig. 11)
baseline.classical_time: not stated; FE work is over 90% of total SIMP time (abstract, §5.4)
baseline.ml_time: not stated; FE work is about 40% of neural-assisted total time (abstract, §5.4)
baseline.training_time: A validation/training procedure is described as approximately 30 min end to end (§3.3); training-only time not separated
baseline.data_generation_cost: SIMP generates training density, displacement and sensitivity maps (§3.2); generation time not separated from the approximately 30 min procedure (§3.3)
baseline.quality_metric: Optimization objective/compliance curves, density and sensitivity maps (§5.1, Figs. 11–12)
baseline.quality_gap: Final structural performance difference reported as less than 10% (§6); casewise numerical FE-verified gap not stated

R1.evidence: §5.1 and §6 compare objective curves and report a structural-performance difference below 10%, but do not establish equal physical-field volume and quality within reported error at the timing point.

R2.evidence: §5.1/§5.4: no hardware, solver type, per-iteration time, or baseline overrun of at least twice an established convergence threshold is shown.

R3.evidence: §3.2–3.3 describes SIMP-generated training data and an approximately 30 min procedure, but the abstract and §5.4 compare run-time shares without separating upstream costs or computing break-even uses.

R4.evidence: §5.1–5.3 compares optimization objective curves and density maps; no separate FE analysis of the returned neural-assisted design or failure-rate accounting is reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: 5 named numerical structures: cantilever, MBB, L-shape, column, rod-supported bridge (§4)

notes: The abstract percentages are not an overall speedup. The publisher PDF was accessible through MDPI's own mdpi-res.com file host after mdpi.com returned HTTP 403.
